title: 2001 AMC 12 Problem 13
statement: The parabola with equation \(y = ax^2 + bx + c\) and vertex \((h, k)\) is reflected about the line \(y = k.\) This results in the parabola with equation \(y = dx^2 + ex + f.\) Which of the following equals \(a + b + c + d + e + f?\)

solutions.text:
The value \(a + b + c\) is the first parabola at \(x = 1,\) and \(d + e + f\) is the reflected parabola at \(x = 1.\)

Reflecting the curve about \(y = k\) replaces each height \(y\) by \(2k - y.\) So at \(x = 1\) the two heights sum to \[ (a + b + c) + (d + e + f) = 2k. \]

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: Note that \(a + b + c\) is the first parabola evaluated at \(x = 1,\) and \(d + e + f\) is the second at \(x = 1\)
Reflecting about \(y = k\) sends the value \(y\) at each \(x\) to \(2k - y\)
